# Standard QR Spec-to-Code Map (ISO/IEC 18004)

This document maps each part of the Standard QR specification (ISO/IEC 18004, versions 1-40) to its implementation. Micro QR and rMQR get their own maps as they are implemented. [QR Symbology Architecture](qrcode-symbologies.md) lists the document set and the shared components.

It is a map, not a copy of the spec. Normative details (bit layouts, formulas, edge-case constraints) and the reasons for implementation choices are in code comments next to the implementation, where they stay in sync with the code. Section numbers below follow the citations in those comments, which use both the `7.x` numbering of ISO/IEC 18004:2015 and the `8.x` numbering of the earlier edition.

## Encoding Pipeline Overview

```
Text ──> Mode analysis ──> Data encoding ──> ECC ──> Interleaving ──> Module placement ──> Masking
```

|---|---|---|
| Section 7.4.1 | Encoding modes (Numeric / Alphanumeric / Byte / Kanji). The analysis selects among the four, and selects Kanji only when the caller sets `AllowKanji` (off by default), the library chose the charset and chose UTF-8 with no byte order mark, and every character has an encoder cell | [EncodingMode.cs](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/EncodingMode.cs), [TextAnalyzer.Analyze](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/TextAnalyzer.cs): scalar classification plus SIMD tiers (x64 AVX2 / SSE2, ARM AdvSimd), selected at runtime. Parity: [TextAnalyzerAdvSimdParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/TextAnalyzerAdvSimdParityTest.cs), [TextAnalyzerX64ParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/TextAnalyzerX64ParityTest.cs), which enter each tier directly because the dispatcher reaches only one tier per machine |
| Section 7.4.3 | Alphanumeric character set (45 characters) and values | [CharacterSets.alphanumericLookup / GetAlphanumericValue](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/CharacterSets.cs), shared across symbologies |
| - | Numeric / Alphanumeric / Byte mode bit stream encoding | [QRBinaryEncoder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRBinaryEncoder.cs) (`WriteNumericData`, `WriteAlphanumericData`, `WriteByteData`) |
| Section 7.4.4 | Character count indicator widths (version 1-9 / 10-26 / 27-40), including Kanji | [EncodingModeExtensions.GetCountIndicatorLength](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/EncodingModeExtensions.cs) |
| Section 7.4 (Kanji mode) | Kanji mode writes 13 bits per character through the shared `ShiftJisKanjiReverseTable`, in both the single-segment and segmented writers, with no ECI header. The generator selects it only with `AllowKanji` (off by default) and when the library chose the charset and chose UTF-8 with no byte order mark: for text whose every character has an encoder cell ([When Kanji mode is written](qrcode-symbologies.md#when-kanji-mode-is-written)) and, under `Optimal`, for the Kanji runs in a Kanji-eligible text's plan, beside runs for its ASCII ([Mixed-mode segmentation](standardqr-encoder.md#mixed-mode-segmentation)) | `QRBinaryEncoder.WriteKanjiData` in [QRBinaryEncoder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRBinaryEncoder.cs). [QRBinaryEncoderKanjiTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/QRBinaryEncoderKanjiTest.cs) checks the writers against a reference built from the standard and the capacity against Table 7's Kanji column, and runs round trips |
| Section 7.4.5 | UTF-8 BOM bytes count toward the character count indicator | [QRCodeGenerator.cs](../../../src/FeatherQR/QRCodeGenerator.cs), [QRBinaryEncoder.GetUtf8Data](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRBinaryEncoder.cs) |
| - | ECI header structure (indicator 4 bits + assignment number) | [EciModeExtensions](../../../src/FeatherQR/EciMode.cs) |
| Section 7.4 (segment sequence) | Several segments in one symbol, each with its own mode and count indicator | [QRSegmentPlanner](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRSegmentPlanner.cs) and [QRBinaryEncoder.WriteSegments](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRBinaryEncoder.cs). The planner, opt-in through the public [QRSegmentation](../../../src/FeatherQR/QRSegmentation.cs), finds the split with the fewest bits and runs the version scan. The cost model is [ModeSegmenter](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ModeSegmenter.cs), shared with Micro QR and rMQR. Rationale and bounds: [Standard QR Encoder](standardqr-encoder.md#mixed-mode-segmentation) |

Reference tests: [QRBinaryEncoderUnitTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/QRBinaryEncoderUnitTest.cs) (includes the canonical "HELLO WORLD" version 1-M example), [QRCodeDecodabilityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/QRCodeDecodabilityTest.cs) (BOM handling, and mixed-mode symbols decoded by ZXing), [QRSegmentPlannerUnitTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/QRSegmentPlannerUnitTest.cs) (the planner's optimum against an independent exhaustive mode assignment, the band widths the scan assumes, the 7,089-character bound with its 4-bit margin, and invariants of the plan's shape), [QRSegmentationTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/QRSegmentationTest.cs) (end to end: never a larger version than single mode, always decodes, byte-identical to single mode when the version does not change, plus the requested-version / range / boost / mask / BOM branches). ## Decoding Pipeline

Design notes (WHAT/WHY and scope tiers) are in [Standard QR Decoder](standardqr-decoder.md).

### Matrix level

```
Module matrix ──> core located ──> version from size ──> format information ──> codeword extraction and unmasking
              ──> codeword deinterleaving ──> Reed-Solomon error correction ──> bit stream decoding ──> text
```

| Spec reference | Topic | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| - | Core located: a module span may include a light quiet zone. The core is the bounding box of the span's dark modules, because a symbol's finder corners are dark. `QRCodeData` input is already the core | [QRCodeDecoder.TryLocateCore](../../../src/FeatherQR/QRCodeDecoder.cs) |
| - | Version from size (size = 17 + 4 · version), then the stages below in order | [QRMatrixDecoder.DecodeMatrix](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRMatrixDecoder.cs) |
| Section 7.8.2 | Format information decoding (Hamming match against all 32 valid patterns) | [FormatInformationDecoder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/FormatInformationDecoder.cs) |
| Section 7.7.3 / 7.8.2 | Codeword extraction and unmasking: the encoder's placement runs are read backwards, four rows per byte. The mask comes from a table of the mask predicates' 12-row, 6-column period | [QRMatrixDecoder.ExtractCodewords](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRMatrixDecoder.Extract.cs). It must match the per-module zigzag walk [ExtractCodewordsReference](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRMatrixDecoder.cs). Parity: [QRMatrixDecoderExtractParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/QRMatrixDecoderExtractParityTest.cs) |
| Section 7.6 | Codeword deinterleaving into RS blocks, the inverse of the interleaver the encoders share. Each block is then corrected, and its data is gathered in block order | [EccBlockDecoder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/BinaryDecoders/EccBlockDecoder.cs), shared with rMQR. [EccBlockDecoderTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/EccBlockDecoderTest.cs) checks that it inverts the interleaver |
| Section 8.5 | Reed-Solomon error correction (syndromes → Berlekamp-Massey → Chien → Forney) | [EccBinaryDecoder.TryCorrect](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/BinaryDecoders/EccBinaryDecoder.cs), shared across symbologies |
| Section 7.4 | Bit stream decoding (mode segments, character count, ECI, Kanji via the shared JIS X 0208 table) | [QRBinaryDecoder.DecodeBitStream](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRBinaryDecoder.cs). The segment payload groups and the byte-charset heuristics are shared with the other symbology decoders through [SegmentDecoders](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/BinaryDecoders/SegmentDecoders.cs) |

Reference tests: [QRCodeDecoderRoundTripTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/QRCodeDecoderRoundTripTest.cs) (encode→decode round-trips, error injection), [EccBinaryDecoderUnitTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/EccBinaryDecoderUnitTest.cs) (correction capacity boundaries), [QRCodeDecoderZXingCrossTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/QRCodeDecoderZXingCrossTest.cs) (cross-validation with an independent encoder), [BitReaderParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/BitReaderParityTest.cs) (the 64-bit window reader against the bit-by-bit definition, shared across symbologies), [ByteSegmentCharsetParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/ByteSegmentCharsetParityTest.cs) (the byte-segment charset rule over an exhaustive corpus of short sequences, for both UTF-8 implementations and the planner's mirror of the rule), [QRBinaryDecoderTruncationTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/QRBinaryDecoderTruncationTest.cs) (every mode cut at every byte).

### Image level

Each pass of the [shared image decode passes](qrcode-symbologies.md#image-decode-passes) runs this path on the finder triple that its finder search selects. The passes and the finder search are drawn on that page.

```
Finder triple
├─ Corner from the triangle: first the corner opposite the longest side, then each other corner whose
│  timing patterns read
│  ├─ Low density: module boundaries read off the timing patterns ──> matrix decode
│  ├─ Finder centres and module sizes
│  ├─ Finders' frame and dimension candidates: the estimate, the timing count, the version information,
│  │  the timing match, the runner-up
│  └─ Each dimension candidate
│     ├─ Alignment search where the frame predicts (version 2+)
│     ├─ Mesh over the alignment lattice (version 7+) ──> matrix decode: here when the search found
│     │  nothing, after the coverage re-read when it anchored the fourth corner
│     ├─ Four-point transform: alignment-anchored, else the parallelogram ──> matrix decode
│     ├─ Coverage re-read (grey levels) ──> matrix decode
│     └─ Parallelogram or frame grid ──> matrix decode, and by coverage (grey levels)
└─ Alternative triples (more than three candidates): each decoded once, from the first of its corners
   whose timing patterns read

Matrix decode: the sampled grid is the core; it goes through the matrix level from version from size on,
then, unless that settles it, transposed (mirror retry)
A read or a verdict on the content settles the triple; no other grid, dimension, corner or triple is tried
```

| Spec reference | Topic | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| - | Global threshold (Otsu), inside the passes ([Image decode passes](qrcode-symbologies.md#image-decode-passes)) | [ImageDecodePasses](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/ImageDecodePasses.cs), shared across symbologies, runs the passes over [QRImageDecoder.SymbolPass](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.cs) (passes: [ImageDecodePassesTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/ImageDecodePassesTest.cs)). [Binarizer](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/Binarizer.cs), shared across symbologies, fills its histogram with a 256-bit tier that counts the two extreme values in registers, an ARM64 tier that does the same without a movemask and spreads dense blocks over four rented sub-histograms, or a scalar walk. The threshold search and the grey levels use only the histogram, so the inverted retry mirrors the first polarity's histogram instead of counting the negative. Parity: [OtsuHistogramParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/OtsuHistogramParityTest.cs) (every bin, entering each tier directly), [OtsuInvertedHistogramTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/OtsuInvertedHistogramTest.cs) (mirrored bins against a count of the negative, and, for each decoder, a light-on-dark symbol with uneven levels), [OtsuThresholdParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/OtsuThresholdParityTest.cs). The condition that enables the grey levels, exact at any pixel count: [GreyLevelsEnableTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/GreyLevelsEnableTest.cs) |
| - | Regional binarization runs when neither polarity of the global threshold reads anything or gives a verdict on the content. Each pixel is compared with the mean black point of the 5 × 5 blocks around its 8 × 8 block. It runs on the positive, then on the negative, each binarized from its own pixels, and each is decoded only when it moves a pixel out of the class that polarity's global threshold gave it. An image of only 0 and 255, or with a side of 32 px or less, is not binarized. It is shared across symbologies, with a 128-bit tier for its three passes. Each attempt runs the decoder's own finder search, as for the global threshold (Micro QR and rMQR: a strided scan, then a full sweep when nothing was read) | [LocalBinarizer](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/LocalBinarizer.cs), [RegionalRetry](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/RegionalRetry.cs). Parity: [LocalBinarizerParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/LocalBinarizerParityTest.cs), retry: [RegionalRetryTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/RegionalRetryTest.cs), decode: [UnevenLightingDecodeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/UnevenLightingDecodeTest.cs) |
| Section 6.3.3 | Finder triple: finder pattern detection (1:1:3:1:1 ratio scan + cross checks) and selection of the best three. The scan is strided and also scans the skipped rows when it selects no triple, or selects a doubtful one after setting once-seen candidates aside ([Image decode passes](qrcode-symbologies.md#image-decode-passes)) | [FinderPatternFinder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/FinderPatternFinder.cs): a scalar row walk plus a bit-identical SIMD mask walk (AVX2 / ARM NEON / portable 128-bit tiers), selected at runtime. Parity: [FinderPatternFinderParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/FinderPatternFinderParityTest.cs). With 256-bit vectors or ARM64 AdvSimd, rows of 32 to 4,095 pixels go to the edge-list kernel instead ([FinderPatternFinder.RowEdges](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/FinderPatternFinder.RowEdges.cs)). It takes every dark run of the row at once and classifies sixteen windows per step, or eight on ARM64, where the word comes from the NEON fold and the verdicts become bits only once a step has a flagged lane. The flagged windows go, in order, to the same follow-up steps. [FinderRowKernelParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/FinderRowKernelParityTest.cs) checks that the three kernels produce one candidate list, and [FinderRowEdgesTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/FinderRowEdgesTest.cs) checks the kernel's two stages against a pixel scan and the scalar ratio checks. The cross-checks measure their five runs through one walk for the column, the row and the diagonal ([FinderPatternFinder.RunWalk](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/FinderPatternFinder.RunWalk.cs)), with the loops it replaced kept as its reference. Parity: [FinderRunWalkParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/FinderRunWalkParityTest.cs). Each line must match 1:1:3:1:1 on its own. The row, measured again through the refined centre, must be within 40 % of the row the scan found, and the column within 5/12 to 12/5 of that row (`IsTotalInWindow`). A column outside the row's 40 % is accepted only when the rising diagonal reads too, along a fourth walk with its own reference. The column and row walks measure the centre run first and stop at the first run that no accepted cross section could have, for either window. [FinderRunBoundsTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/FinderRunBoundsTest.cs) checks these bounds against the ratio checks, and [FinderCrossCheckParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/FinderCrossCheckParityTest.cs) checks the cross-check through both walks. A line that fails the ratio is read again by the distances between its like edges, within the row's 40 %, unless its dark runs are longer than their modules where the row's are shorter, or the reverse, and a finder read this way must also read along its rising diagonal: [FinderLikeEdgesTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/FinderLikeEdgesTest.cs), [SpreadRingDecodeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/SpreadRingDecodeTest.cs) |
| - | Corner from the triangle: the vertex opposite the longest side of the centres' triangle is the top-left finder, and the cross product tells the other two apart. On a symbol tilted about both axes toward the top-left finder past about 43 % keystone, a leg of the finder triangle is longer than its hypotenuse, so the vertex opposite the longest side is another finder. When the decode from the shape's corner does not settle, each other corner is therefore decoded if its timing patterns read through its own frame. [TwoAxisTiltDecodeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/TwoAxisTiltDecodeTest.cs) covers the decode of renders (red on the commit before and with each piece switched off), a photograph tilted toward one of its finders at four turns, the premise (a leg of the drawn triangle longer than its hypotenuse, so the shape names another corner, and timing patterns that read from the drawn corner and not from the shape's), the drawn corner found by its timing patterns whichever order the triple comes in, a triple none of whose corners reads, a damaged render, a flat symbol whose timing patterns read from its corner only, the column window's margin under a stretch off the finder's axes, and the tilted renderer against its own geometry. [FinderTripleCornersTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/FinderTripleCornersTest.cs) checks which corners are decoded, for the selected triple and the alternatives, recording them through a stand-in for the timing check and the decode (`ICornerAttempt`), so a corner decoded without its timing patterns reading fails a test | [QRImageDecoder.OrderFinderPatterns, DecodeTriple, TryCornerByTimingPatterns, DecodeAlternativeTriples](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.cs) |
| - | Low density: a crisp symbol, upright or turned by a right angle, whose top-left finder measures under 1.75 px per module is read through a table of module boundaries, taken from its two timing patterns and the finders' own lines, instead of a fitted transform. This read is tried first for every corner and needs both timing lines to read as timing patterns of the same dimension | [QRImageDecoder.DecodeThroughTimingFrame, TryReadModuleBoundaries](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.cs), [ModuleBoundaryReader](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/ModuleBoundaryReader.cs), shared across symbologies. Decode and refusals: [ModuleBoundaryReaderTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/ModuleBoundaryReaderTest.cs). Crisp renders between 1 and 1.5 px/module: [FractionalLowDensityDecodeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/FractionalLowDensityDecodeTest.cs) |
| - | Finder centres and module sizes: the module size is measured at both ends of each finder line, along the line, because an image row measures a turned finder up to √2 times too long. On an image with grey levels, each centre moves to the centroid of its centre square's darkness, and the sizes are measured again to sub-pixel edges | [QRImageDecoder.MeasureModuleSizes, RefineFinderCentres](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.cs), [FinderAxisEstimator](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/FinderAxisEstimator.cs) and [ConcentricCentroid](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/ConcentricCentroid.cs), shared across symbologies. The centroid: [ConcentricCentroidTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/ConcentricCentroidTest.cs) |
| - | Finders' frame and dimension candidates: the frame is the plane fixed by the three finder centres and the module sizes at the ends of the two finder lines. It predicts where the alignment pattern is searched, the timing match runs through it, and it is sampled itself when nothing anchored the fourth corner. The estimate counts each finder line's modules. Where the frame foreshortens, it divides each line's length by the geometric mean of the line's two end sizes, which gives the count the frame implies. The count is snapped to a version, keeping the runner-up. When the estimate's grids fail, three candidates follow in order: the timing count (the dark runs of both timing patterns), the version information read from the first candidate's four-point grid (version 7+), and the timing match (the dimension near the estimate whose grid puts both timing patterns on alternating modules through the frame). The runner-up comes last. Each is tried only when it names a dimension not yet tried. When no valid dimension is near the estimate, the candidates start with the timing count, or, failing that, with the timing match | [QRImageDecoder.FinderFrame](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.FinderFrame.cs), [QRImageDecoder.EstimateModules, TryEstimateDimension, CountTimingDimension, ReadVersionDimension, MatchTimingDimension](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.cs). Parity with a plane, and the count and the timing match against a full count: [FinderFrameTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/FinderFrameTest.cs). The timing count: [TimingPatternDimensionTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/TimingPatternDimensionTest.cs). The version information: [VersionInformationReadTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/VersionInformationReadTest.cs). Past 20 % keystone, red on the commit before and with each mechanism switched off: [KeystoneFinderDecodeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/KeystoneFinderDecodeTest.cs) |
| Section 6.3.6 / Annex E | Alignment search: the bottom-right alignment pattern (version 2+) is searched in widening windows where the finders' frame predicts it, and along the frame's axes there. It is detected by a light-dark-light core plus a border-ring check along the grid axes, and its centre is refined like the finders' centres | [QRImageDecoder.BuildGridTransform](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.cs), [AlignmentPatternFinder](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/AlignmentPatternFinder.cs): a scalar row walk plus a result-identical SIMD mask walk (AVX2 / ARM NEON / portable 128-bit tiers), selected at runtime. Parity: [AlignmentPatternFinderParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/AlignmentPatternFinderParityTest.cs) |
| - | Mesh over the alignment lattice: version 7+, used when at least half of the searched nodes are found, and bilinear over the lattice. From version 14, the edge lines are extrapolated from the interior nodes. For versions 7 to 13, which have two interior nodes per line, the edge lines and any interior node not found are placed by the plane that best fits the finder centres and the nodes found. The mesh is decoded before the four-point transform when the alignment search found nothing. When the search anchored the fourth corner, the mesh is decoded after the anchored transform and its coverage re-read, because a flat symbol is one projective map, which the anchored transform fits and the mesh only interpolates | [QRImageDecoder.TryBuildSampleMesh, TryBuildSmallSampleMesh](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.cs), [ProjectiveFit](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/ProjectiveFit.cs) (shared with rMQR), [QRImageDecoder.SampleGridPiecewise](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.PiecewiseSampling.cs). The sampler's AVX2 tier (net8.0+, eight modules per step), ARM64 tier (four lanes, two steps per loop body) and portable column-table tier must all match the per-module loop `SampleGridPiecewiseScalar` pixel for pixel. Parity: [SampleGridPiecewiseParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/SampleGridPiecewiseParityTest.cs) |
| - | Four-point transform and sampling: the transform goes through the three finder centres and the alignment centre, or through the parallelogram's fourth corner when no alignment pattern anchors it | [PerspectiveTransform](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/PerspectiveTransform.cs), shared across symbologies. [PerspectiveGridSampler](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/PerspectiveGridSampler.cs), shared with Micro QR: a scalar loop plus bit-identical SIMD row kernels (AVX2 / portable 128-bit for ARM NEON and WASM), selected at runtime. Parity: [PerspectiveGridSamplerParityTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/Shared/PerspectiveGridSamplerParityTest.cs) |
| - | Coverage re-read: on an image with grey levels, a grid that failed (the four-point grid, the parallelogram after an anchored grid, or the finders' frame grid) is read again: each module's luminance is interpolated at its centre and split halfway between the two levels, and the result is decoded only when that changes a module | [QRImageDecoder.DecodeByCoverage, SampleGridByCoverage](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.cs), [LuminanceSampler](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/LuminanceSampler.cs), shared across symbologies. No test calls it directly |
| - | Parallelogram or frame grid: after an alignment-anchored grid fails, the decoder tries the grid through the parallelogram of the three centres. When nothing anchored the fourth corner and the frame foreshortens, it tries the frame's own grid. Each is decoded only when it samples different modules, then read again by coverage on an image with grey levels. Neither is tried at the runner-up dimension | [QRImageDecoder.BuildParallelogramTransform, DecodeOtherGrid](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.cs), [FinderFrame.Transform](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.FinderFrame.cs). Keystone past what the parallelogram anchors: [KeystoneFrameDecodeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/KeystoneFrameDecodeTest.cs) |
| - | Alternative triples: when the selected triple does not settle and the list holds more than three candidates, up to two other triples are tried, ranked by the height in modules over which their least confirmed member was confirmed, then by the selection score. Each is decoded once, from the first of its corners whose timing patterns read through its own frame | [QRImageDecoder.DecodeAlternativeTriples](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.cs), [FinderPatternFinder.AlternativeTriples](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/FinderPatternFinder.Alternatives.cs). The order: [FinderAlternativeTriplesTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/FinderAlternativeTriplesTest.cs). Which corners are decoded: [FinderTripleCornersTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/FinderTripleCornersTest.cs) |
| - | Matrix decode and mirror retry: every sampled grid is the core and goes through the matrix level from version from size on. A grid that does not settle is decoded again transposed, because a mirrored capture has the same finders and a transposed grid. A read or a verdict on the content settles the triple, and no other grid, dimension, corner or triple is tried | [QRImageDecoder.DecodeWithMirrorRetry](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/StandardQR/QRImageDecoder.cs). Each level of the search keeps its result in [SearchResult](../../../src/FeatherQR/Internals/ImageDecoders/SearchResult.cs) (`ReportRule.MainPath`), shared across symbologies. A mirrored image: [QRCodeDecoderImageTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/QRCodeDecoderImageTest.cs) (`Decode_MirroredImage`) |

Reference tests: [QRCodeDecoderImageTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/QRCodeDecoderImageTest.cs) (rotation/mirror/scale/inversion image cases), [QRCodeDecoderPerspectiveTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/QRCodeDecoderPerspectiveTest.cs) (keystone envelope, rotation+perspective combinations), [KeystoneFrameDecodeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/KeystoneFrameDecodeTest.cs) (keystone past what the parallelogram of the finders anchors, on synthetic images and zxing-cpp's real images, with corners within half a module), [SmallLatticeMeshDecodeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/SmallLatticeMeshDecodeTest.cs) (versions 7 to 13 bowed off the plane, synthetic and real), [ParallelogramCoverageDecodeTest](../../../tests/FeatherQR.Tests/StandardQr/ParallelogramCoverageDecodeTest.cs) (round modules whose parallelogram reads only by coverage).

## Maintenance Notes

- When adding or moving a spec-referenced implementation, update this map. Keep details (bit layouts, formulas, constraints) in the code comment next to the implementation, not here.
- Parity tests keep a naive reference implementation of the spec text. They are the executable form of the specification and should stay simple even when the production kernels change.
- Components marked "shared across symbologies" live outside `Internals/StandardQR`. The shared/per-symbology split is defined in [QR Symbology Architecture](qrcode-symbologies.md).
- A change that adds, removes or reorders a decode stage or retry also updates this map's decode diagrams, the image decoder's pipeline remarks and the decode figures in the [design record](standardqr-decoder.md#image-decode-figures). For the figures, rerun `dotnet run tools/decode_figures.cs -- .github/docs/images`, then recheck each figure's box states and notes against the code. A change inside a stage, such as a tolerance or a gate, can also flip a box's state, and the tool checks the decodes, not the box states.
